sections.overview: The Greater Crested Tern is a large coastal tern distributed from southern Africa across the Indian Ocean to the western Pacific.
sections.identification: It has a shaggy black crest, grey upperparts, white underparts and a long yellow bill. Compare it with the Sandwich Tern (T. sandvicensis), whose bill is black with a yellow tip; see that profile.
sections.habitat: It nests on offshore sandy, rocky or coral islands and also uses coastal waters, estuaries and lagoons.
sections.diet: It feeds mainly on small fish, caught by shallow plunge-dives; squid and crabs are also taken.
sections.behavior: It may occur alone or in flocks and forms noisy colonies to breed; many populations remain near nesting areas.
sections.reproduction: Pairs nest on the ground in a shallow scrape, usually laying one egg in Australia and one or two in other regions.
sections.ecology: Its fish-based diet and island colonies tie it to shallow coastal waters and nearby marine prey.
sections.conservation: It is not globally threatened overall, though dense colonies can be locally vulnerable to disturbance and predators.
